title: Unemployment Insurance Appeals In-Person Sessions — Computing the Session Date and Notice Period
content:
The in-person session notice period under Unemployment Insurance Appeals is the number of calendar days from today, the day the party books the session and its notice is mailed, to the in-person session date. The in-person session date is the set hearing date moved later by the room block gap. The room block gap is the standard room block days, **4** calendar days. An in-person session date that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday moves to the following Monday.

## Input, judgement, output

- **Input:** today's date; the hearing date currently set on the appeal record.
- **Date found:** the set hearing date moved 4 calendar days later.
- **Judgement:** is the date found a Saturday (move 2 days) or a Sunday (move 1 day) — to the following Monday — or another weekday (stands)?
- **Output:** the notice period, the calendar days from today (day 0) to the session date; equivalently, the total of the days from today to the set hearing date, the 4-day room block gap and any weekend move.

## Worked computations (hypothetical inputs; today is Wednesday 15 April 2026)

| Set hearing date | Days from today | Date found | Weekend move | Session date | Notice period |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monday 4 May 2026 | 19 | Friday 8 May | none | Friday 8 May | 23 days |
| Wednesday 6 May 2026 | 21 | Sunday 10 May | 1 day | Monday 11 May | 26 days |
| Tuesday 28 April 2026 | 13 | Saturday 2 May | 2 days | Monday 4 May | 19 days |

Every count is in calendar days, and the session date is always counted from today, the booking day.
